text:
The change moves stage-a1 (10.101.2.10, tenantA-stage) from VLAN 111 to VLAN 110 on leaf1 ge2. The ticket doesn't say what VLAN 110 is. The hosts list suggests tenantA-web is 10.101.1.x (likely VLAN 110) and tenantA-stage is 10.101.2.x (likely VLAN 111), so this looks like a stage-a1 move into the web segment, possibly a mistake. The plan has to verify the intended outcome and catch collateral changes.

Since the target VLAN is unknown, I use "like" tests against both candidate reference hosts. If the move is correct, stage-a1 would match web-a1, so that test passes. If it was meant to stay stage-like, a like test against stage-b1 would show the difference. Unchanged-access checks cover the other hosts so that no collateral damage goes unnoticed.

```json
{"tests": [
  {"t":"like","host":"stage-a1","as":"web-a1"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"dns-dc1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"backup1","svc":"tcp/22","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"db-a1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"app-a1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"db-b1","svc":"*","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"web-b1","svc":"*","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-a1","dst":"stage-b1","svc":"*","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"tcp/22","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"tcp/22","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-a1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"app-a1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"db-a1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-a1","dst":"app-a1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-a1","dst":"db-a1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-b1","dst":"db-b1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"stage-b1","dst":"db-b1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"leaf1","prefix":"10.101.2.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"leaf1","prefix":"10.101.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"border1","prefix":"10.101.2.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"spine1","prefix":"10.101.2.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"leaf1","b":"spine1","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"leaf1","b":"spine2","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"stage-a1","dst":"app-a1","size":9000,"expect":"pass"}
]}
```

Notes for the reviewer:
- The first test is the key one. It passes only if VLAN 110 gives stage-a1 the same access as web-a1. If this is a typo for VLAN 111 and stage-a1 is meant to keep its stage access, expect that test to fail, along with the "unchanged" tests for stage-a1's reach and the 10.101.2.0/24 routes. A failure there means the change should be rejected.
- If VLAN 110 is a genuinely new or different VLAN, the "unchanged" reach tests show what access stage-a1 gained or lost, and the ticket should state the intended access policy.
